text: These were my first pair of Bluetooth headphones and honestly I wasn't impressed. They didn't work very well and the sound was muffled. Wouldn't spend your money on these.

These caught my attention because of the cool led inside the charging case. Practical use though they kind of fell short. The sound wasn’t at all what I had hoped. I just needed enough volume to drown out the gyms sound system. But even outside without music blaring it was still oddly hard to hear. The ear hooks were a little too weak for my liking. I prefer something a bit more ridged since I’m using these as gym headphones. Over these weren’t terrible they were just ok. For my use (gym sessions) it didn’t quite fit the bill. But I think if you need a pair to have laying around as a backup these are priced right and a decent choice.

no major problems so far, but the left ear is a bit quieter than the right, and the over-all sound quality is poor. I had no trouble setting it up, they are comfortable and easy to use, but at the end of the day, they just don't sound good. I understand not being able to produce a heavy bass in a wireless earbud, but every bass track on pop & rock songs i have listened to so far has either been muffled to the point of being inaudible, or just produced a crackly static.

TL:DR : good physical design, crap audio.

UPDATE: Customer service contacted me and said my pair seems to be defective and offered to send me an updated pair. changed from 2 star to 3 for good customer service

These headphones have a substandard sound, bass, and spatial field. The bass is not only recessed and somewhat muddy, it sits in the middle while the treble is in outer space at the edges and the sound is neither clear, pleasant nor coordinated. Also the earcups are just a little small and they're not as comfortable or well-made as, say, Anker. For wireless headphones these don't sound good. For Sony they're worse. For the price they're horrible.

For a fraction of the price you can get Boltune, Mpow or any number of brands that are better built, more comfortable, and sound *much* better.

I like the Mpow 059/059+ myself.

For the price I paid I didn't have high expectations, but I did expect them to work. To be completely honest, I feel like I was duped into ordering these because of the good comments. I can only get them to work with 1 tablet and my laptop, but not either of my cell phones. The right ear is very very quiet, I'd say about 10-20% the volume of the left side.

Also there is an issue with audio skipping and lagging.

The one plus, I would say, is that they are comfortable in my ears (and I have problems finding earbuds that fit comfortably)

I definitely prefer to use Bluetooth earbuds any day over wired, but sometimes it can't be helped.  Such as times when my Bluetooth earbuds weren't charged.  The sound of these is o.k. but not what you'd be getting from a high end pair.  I teach classical guitar so my acid test for any earbud is playing that and seeing how it sounds.  I'm doing it now and the trebles come through o.k. but the bass is pretty weak.  These will be good to keep a pair in my car or purse for those times when my Bluetooths won't work for whatever reasons.  The volume doesn't work so it has to be adjusted on the device they're plugged into.  They come with extra earbud covers and they feel fine in my female ears the way they are.  I don't know what these cost as of this review but I wouldn't want to pay more than $15.00 for them.

I STRONGLY recommend NOT buying this.  The microphone sounds like there is a bad ground.  Nothing but a loud hum/buzz.  The headset itself is comfortable and sound quality is good.  The mic though... unusable.

After 4 months of careful use, only one speaker works. Apparently the connection of the cord to the headset is flimsy and there was static from day one. But now only one speaker works and that is very irritating.

I wear a headset for the better part of a day. I like to use headsets rather than the phone handset because it keeps my hands free.

These definitely do the job with noise cancelling and the volume control works very well. I've been told once or twice that people have trouble hearing me at times, but since I don't know if that's the headset or their phones, I deducted a single star.

My only complaint is the clip that puts the volume control and mute button together is very difficult to hook onto anything other than very thin fabric. I have to struggle to get it on and off my jacket during the day. My suggestion to the manufacturer, make the clip easier to slide fabric into or make it a clip that opens.

Decent audio but not great for critical listening. They aren't noise canceling and they don't isolate much better than any rubber buds. I enjoy the battery life and case with extra battery. Also the wireless charging.
So love this headset! Easy to put on. Sound quality is excellent and super easy to charge when dead. Totally recommend buying

I'm a software developer who works in a cubicle world with the heating system droning on above the ceiling (we're on the top floor of an office building - the HVAC is on the roof). These headphones provide an oasis of silence! The noise cancellation *seems* to be a cut above the others I've tried (Beats Studio at Target and a Sony set at Costco) although it's not really fair to compare as I didn't try the Bose under the same condition as the others (i.e. in a noisy store).

How good is it? The droning AC noise is completely gone. Voices I can still hear - until I play music. Even at low/moderate playback volume, voices are barely audible. People have to pat me on the back if they want my attention.

Comfort is excellent. I wear them on-and-off all day without problems. I imagine people with big ears might be less comfortable.

Power: the headphones use a single AAA battery. Keeping in mind that I maybe play music for 2-3 hours every day, the battery seems to last 2-3 weeks. As others have noted, these headphones will not work (i.e. play music) without power.

My one nitpick (and the reason I can't give it 5 stars) is the god-awful chord. It's some cheap plasticky material that I continually have to unravel by dangling the headphones by the plug end and letting the headphones rotate. It's really quite pathetic to put such cheap cr$p on $300 headphones - shame on Bose for not correcting this. Is it really going to affect your profitability so much you can't do something like the $20 Apple headphones that come with every iPhone (they're more rubberized and don't seem to get raveled).

Update for iPhone/iPad/iPod users: with iOS 7, Apple introduced a new way to invoke Siri (Apple's voice assistant) - instead of holding down the home button (or center button on the headphones) until you hear the Siri confirmation sound and then asking Siri your question and then waiting for Siri to accept your input, with iOS 7, you can keep the button pressed until you're finished talking - and avoid the delay Siri normally waits to know you're done with talking. It's a very useful feature.....and, it doesn't work with the Bose inline chord button :-( Not really Bose's fault, I guess, but I thought it worth mentioning.

Good headphones for the money.  Sound is not as good as an expensive pair but they are nice in that they fold.  They have been pretty durable my son used them for school and then were brought back home and we have used them around.  They are light/plastic so quality is what you would expect in this price range.

Pros:
- sound quality is good
- my coworkers can hear me well on conference calls
- the price is affordable

Cons:

- putting them in and taking them out can both cause random things on my phone to start playing, even if no apps were open (I hate this!)

A few things I am not too happy about: First, the earbud is hard and not at all pliable or flexible which makes it not only uncomfortable in the ear, but the buds tend to slowly slide out of the ear and can easily fall out at that point. They are difficult to remove from the case - bad design in my opinion.

The sound is great. The instructions are so tiny - not small, but TINY - that they are impossible to read without a magnifier.

I like listening to music while I am reading.  I bought a green Kindle cover and these earphones go nicely with it.  The sound is good, they are comfortable and portable.  You can't beat these for the price!

I think I have finally found an above average headset. The sound quality is pretty great but what I love the most is how long a full charge lasts. I clocked it at 25 hours of straight music. Yep, even when I slept. I  can’t sleep without music but my husband needs silence. I usual put in my earbuds but those were constantly falling out and getting lost. I didn’t think I could sleep with big headphones on and have tried a few times with no luck. I can not believe how comfortable these are. I couldn’t even tell I had them on. This was so simple to pair and I have these paired to six separate devices and they work great. The functions are easy to use and the noise canceling is 100% effective. I love these and they are my number one choice in my Bluetooth devices.

These are ok. My daughter is 6 and they look very bulky on her. She said they are too big for her - they seem wide making them a bit bulky. She picked them out because she liked the color and the pony on them, the style and material quality isnt the greatest, but the sound quality is pretty good.

My daughter says they’re perfect. Retractable, comfortable, noise canceling, surround sound, and you’re able to change to the next song by clicking a side button. She absolutely loves the style as well! Great quality at a great price!

I bought these to see what all the fuss was about. While aimlessly wandering the internet, I came across talk about KZ ATE's. I paraphrase one review that kept popping up in all the sources; I read, "these $15 earphones feel and sound like $50+ ones." At first I was skeptical as I own a pair of Bose QuietComfort i20's (the noise canceling earphones at $323.98, (CA tax included)), and wanted to compare the two. To my surprise, they are as the internet (collectively) said it does sound like a more expensive pair of earphones. The sound quality on these KZ's are quiet nice and hold a better base than my beloved Bose do but, for me, they do tend to fall out when not in a stationary position, i.e. walking around, running, biking, etc. They look like they cost more also, feels expensive and have a reassuring weight to them. Overall, these are a good buy and well worth it compared to more expensive earphones. (I also recommend the Bose, noise cancelation is worth it when the world gets a bit too overwhelming and all you want is some peace & quiet.. and music.)

You can fix this by upgrading to the firmer foam tips, but then the buds won't fit in the case so you have to take the tips off every time you want to put them away.

Because they have different sizes to choose from, you don't have to worry about the discomfort of extra pressure or too little security while enjoying your favorite music and programs! Sennheiser is an excellent brand for a durable, long-lasting purchase that you will not ever regret and these are well worth the buy. Just connect and GO!

JBL is my favorite brand of headphones. They usually last a long time and when they go bad I just buy another pair. I was a little worried because of the reviews but I've had these headphones for a while and they've worked excellently.

Each side clicks slightly as it slides up and down to adjust head sizes but it’s very easy for them to slide and makes it annoying to be constantly adjusting them.

I was a little skeptical because I haven't exactly been sold on wireless ear buds. I have these inexpensive Amazon basic ear buds that have been solid for me for almost a year now and I also already have a fitbit that I like very much that fits my admittedly modest fitness needs. That said, I was curious about this item so I wanted to try it out and I was pleasantly surprised and impressed by Jabra Elite Sport True-Wireless Bluetooth Stereo Earbuds. They were well packaged. I like that it has a selection of earbuds (small, medium, and large). They are comfortable to wear and they stayed put as well. App was easy to install on my iPhone and set up and so far, it is registering good readings. Bonus is that not only did the earbuds pick up as accessible for my iPhone, it also paired with my PC so I like that flexibility. It is on the pricey side (for me, anyway) and that is probably the main drawback so far that I can see for someone with my budget. Yet, now that I have tried it, it is a really nice to have item and I think for someone who is more serious and 'elite' with his/her fitness goals, he/she would probably find more pertinent use for it.

The Apple AirPods Pro are a definite step up from the regular AirPods, stay in your ears well (the Beats Fit Pro does slightly better here, but the microphone is not as good as on the AirPods Pro), have good noise cancellation (Bose and Sony might be a tad better, but these are very good), and excellent microphone pickup.  If you are going to be in a loot of phone calls, eMeetings (Zoom, Webex, Facetime, etc.) these are very much the ones to get.  About the only thing these are not good for would be high head movement activities (athletics), there the Beats Fit Pro does better, but these are on a par or better than the competitive Sony or Bose variants (which are larger, so easier to dislodge).  Also, once paired with Apple devices, you can just move them around to be used with whatever you happen to be doing, iPad or iPhone or MacBook, they autoswitch, don't have to be re-paired, and also handle Siri commands.

These are great com units. We have more than one set and will likely be getting more. I am not sure about the headpieces though. The staff says they are a little uncomfy but they still use them and aren't demanding new headsets... Yet. The range is more than what we need. I use them on medium power for the range to help save on the battery because I need them to last a full weekend of use. I like how if the battery does drain, I can always fall back on AAs. The rechargeable feature is really nice and in the event of power failure and battery dying we can also charge them in the cars. The weaker Midland coms that we have work well with these but their range isn't as good. They sometimes will cut out on the edges of the location we work in. These ones don't have that problem though. They beep for a bit to warn of low battery. Giving you plenty of time to get back to where you can get a recharge or replacement battery.

These headphones were very nice. They were easy to use. They were comfortable for my daughter. I really like that they have noise cancellation. The quality was fantastic. They worked great. They were attractive. I would recommend them.

These are now my most favorite headphones. They are noise cancelling and you can pair them with two devices at the same time. You get about 30 hours of listening time, which is great for me, because I listen to podcasts at night and don't want to have to fumble around for ear buds when my headphone runs out - which I have had to do in the past. What is really cool about these headphones, besides being blue tooth and noise cancelling, is that you can remove them and they stop playing your music or podcasts until you put them back on again. This also comes with an app that you download for android or iPhone and with that, you can set up to play radio or spotify to wake you up and a number of other tasks. I am still looking into the app. I highly recommend that you watch the video on the Amazon page to get a better idea on how to set these up and what they can do. The transparency allows you to pause while you listen to what is going on inside the room.

I love wrap around your ear headphones. They’re much more comfortable in my opinion.

The design of these is nice and they’re easy to use. The case is nice as well for charging and keeping them together when you’re not wearing them.

I have some really great MEE headphones - my favorite for long stretches of music listening. Those are A151 and I recommend those for that application.
